periods.analysis: Our directory lists 41 free and low-cost food sites, and 15.8% of surveyed adults say they worry about running out of food, which sets the baseline. School food programs are running at only nine schools because several campuses lack volunteer coordinators, and Dune Avenue and Seagrove have few sites within walking distance.
periods.recommendations: Recruit school volunteer coordinators with the district and scout a mobile distribution stop for Seagrove.

periods.analysis: Sites grew to 44 and school programs to 12 after the district named a staff contact for school pantries in April, which cleared the spring backlog. Food worry dipped slightly to 15.1%, a change too small to read as a trend. Cold storage at schools is the next constraint.
periods.recommendations: Prepare the back-to-school launch at five more schools and open the Seagrove mobile stop.

periods.analysis: The resource directory lists 49 free and low-cost food sites, up from 41 in Q1, and 17 schools now run weekend packs, care closets or share tables. The share of adults worried about running out of food dipped from 15.8% to 14.6% over the baseline year. Dune Avenue and Seagrove remain the longest walks to a site and drive the Q4 siting plan.
periods.recommendations: Site a new distribution in Dune Avenue and fund cold storage for the remaining schools.
